scope: Proposition 7.7 (Passage to the four metric fluxes) of the manuscript “The nonmaximal anti-de Sitter Penrose Inequality and original-data rigidity” (preprints/The-nonmaximal-anti-de-Sitter-Penrose-Inequality-and-original-data-rigidity-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9e2b9ba2768918dc), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 89. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose g has an asymptotically hyperbolic end with background b and four finite metric fluxes pa(g), a = 0, 1, 2, 3, in the designated chart, as defined in Equation (2.9). Assume that, outside a compact set, n is a constant and λ = q A2 0 + r2, with fixed A0 > 0. Assume the differentiated end bounds g − b = O2(r−κ ), K = O1(r−κ ), t = O2(r−s ), w = O2(r−β ), κ > 3 2 , s > 3 2 , β > 3 2 , κ + β > 3. (7.35) Finally, suppose that for some δ > 0, Rb g + 6 = O(r−3−δ ). (7.36) Then all four metric fluxes of b g exist and are finite. For each a = 0, 1, 2, 3, pa(b g) − pa(g) = − 1 2π lim r→∞ ˆ Sr (Va dt − t dVa)(νb) dAb. (7.37) Moreover, V∗ = 4(λ∇gt − t∇gλ) + o(r−2 ), (7.38) and the time-component identity is p0(b g) − p0(g) = − 1 8π lim r→∞ ˆ Sr g(V∗, νg) dAg. (7.39)
